In mathematics, specifically in [[order theory]] and [[functional analysis]], an '''abstract ''L''-space''', an '''AL-space''', or an '''abstract Lebesgue space''' is a [[Banach lattice]] <math>(X, \| \cdot \|)</math> whose norm is additive on the positive cone of ''X''.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=242–250}}

In [[probability theory]], it means the [[standard probability space]].<ref>{{citation |title=Stationary Stochastic Processes|author=Takeyuki Hida|page=21}}</ref>

== Examples ==

The strong dual of an [[AM-space]] with unit is an AL-space.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=242–250}}  

== Properties ==

The reason for the name abstract ''L''-space is because every AL-space is isomorphic (as a Banach lattice) with some subspace of <math>L^1(\mu).</math>{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=242–250}}
Every AL-space ''X'' is an [[order complete]] [[vector lattice]] of [[Minimal vector lattice|minimal type]]; 
however, the [[Order dual (functional analysis)|order dual]] of ''X'', denoted by ''X''<sup>+</sup>, is ''not'' of minimal type unless ''X'' is finite-dimensional.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=242–250}}  
Each order interval in an AL-space is weakly compact.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=242–250}}

The strong dual of an AL-space is an [[AM-space]] with unit.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=242–250}} 
The continuous dual space <math>X^{\prime}</math> (which is equal to ''X''<sup>+</sup>) of an AL-space ''X'' is a [[Banach lattice]] that can be identified with <math>C_{\R} ( K )</math>, where ''K'' is a compact [[extremally disconnected]] topological space; 
furthermore, under the evaluation map, ''X'' is isomorphic with the band of all real [[Radon measure]]s 𝜇 on ''K'' such that for every [[majorized]] and directed subset ''S'' of <math>C_{\R} ( K ),</math> we have <math>\lim_{f \in S} \mu ( f ) = \mu ( \sup S ).</math>{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=242–250}}
